mainTopic: What splits one field into separate fields: the פאה list, the טומאה case (רבי אליעזר's ספק ביאה rule), and the dispute over whether this applies to שבת
overview: Earlier, the גמרא discussed whether a boundary (מצר) or a sea squill (חצב) splits a field into separate fields, and רבין quoted רבי יוחנן that it does for פאה and for טומאה. The amud opens by finishing the list of things that divide a field for פאה: roads and paths, public or private. It then asks what the טומאה case is and answers with a משנה in טהרות about a man who walked in a valley but does not know whether he entered the field with the טומאה. רבי אליעזר rules him טהור, because a doubt whether one entered (ספק ביאה) is טהור, while a doubt whether one touched (ספק מגע) is טמא. So whether the area counts as a separate field changes the ruling. The גמרא infers from רבין's wording that the divider does not count for שבת. רבא disagrees and says it counts even for שבת. He brings a ברייתא about carrying two halves of a dried fig in one or two periods of forgetting. רבי יוסי's opinion in that ברייתא begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rest of the list of things that divide a field for פאה
steps.stepSummary: The list of dividers for פאה is completed: public and private roads, and public and private paths that are used all year round.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a public road, and a private road, and a public path, and a private path that is permanent, used both in the summer and in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of things that split a field into separate fields, so that each part needs its own פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roads and paths, whether public or private, count as dividers. A private path counts only if it is קבוע, meaning people use it all year, both summer and winter. This list is the background for the question of whether a מצר or חצב also divides.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor; each separate field needs its own
A path, narrower than a road

phrases.english: and a public road, and a private road,
and a public path, and a permanent private path

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וּבֵין בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: whether in the summer or in the rainy season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of field dividers from before this section began
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Public and private roads, public paths, and permanent private paths all divide a field for פאה.

steps.title: What is the טומאה case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law of טומאה depends on whether an area counts as one field or two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: when רבין said a divider matters for טומאה, which case did he mean? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פאה it is easy to see why dividing a field matters, since each field needs its own corner. With טומאה it is less obvious, so the גמרא asks for the specific case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to identify the case

phrases.english: Impurity: what is it?
phrases.notes: He's asking which case of טומאה depends on whether this counts as one field or two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פאה list to explaining the טומאה side of רבין's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which טומאה law is affected by whether an area is a separate field

steps.title: The man unsure whether he entered the impure field
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from a משנה: a man walked in a valley in winter and does not know whether he entered the field where the טומאה was. רבי אליעזר says he is טהור; the חכמים say he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone who enters a valley during the rainy season, and there is impurity in a certain field. He says, 'I walked to that place, but I do not know whether I entered that spot or not.' רבי אליעזר rules him pure, and the חכמים rule him impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a משנה where whether something counts as a separate field changes the ruling on טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man knows he was in the valley but is unsure whether he entered the specific field with the טומאה. רבי אליעזר rules him טהור and the חכמים rule him טמא. The next step explains רבי אליעזר's reasoning, and that reasoning is why a divider matters.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two places: the man is sure he was in the valley. His doubt is only about whether he went into the specific field where the טומאה was.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who enters a valley during the rainy season,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in טהרות 6:5.

phrases.english: and there is impurity in a certain field,
and he said: I walked to that place,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם נִכְנַסְתִּי לְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם וְאִם לָאו –
phrases.english: but I do not know whether I entered that spot or not,
Rabbi Eliezer rules him pure, and the Rabbis rule him impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by quoting a משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טומאה case is the משנה about a man unsure whether he entered the field with טומאה, where רבי אליעזר rules him טהור.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's rule: doubt about entering versus doubt about touching
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's reason: if it is unsure whether he entered, he is טהור; if he surely entered and is only unsure whether he touched the טומאה, he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אליעזר used to say: A doubt about entering means pure. A doubt about touching impurity means impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains why רבי אליעזר rules the man טהור: he draws a line between being unsure whether you entered and being unsure whether you touched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you surely entered the impure area and only doubt whether you touched the טומאה, you are טמא. If you doubt whether you entered at all, you are טהור. So it matters whether the impure spot counts as its own separate field. If a divider makes it separate, walking in the valley is not the same as entering that field, and the doubt becomes ספק ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether one entered the area
A doubt whether one touched the impure thing

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר: unsure whether you entered means טהור; sure you entered but unsure whether you touched means טמא. That is why a divider that makes a separate field matters for טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the link back to רבין: a divider decides whether the doubt counts as ספק ביאה (טהור) or ספק מגע (טמא).

phrases.english: For Rabbi Eliezer used to say:
A doubt about entering: pure,
a doubt about touching impurity: impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ספק ביאה is טהור and ספק מגע is טמא, so whether the impure area is a separate field decides the case.

steps.title: The divider does not count for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that even according to רבין, a מצר or חצב divides only for פאה and טומאה, not for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבין's wording: a boundary or sea squill divides fields for פאה and טומאה, but not for the laws of שבת. This sets up רבא's disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבין named only פאה and טומאה, the גמרא understands that he left out שבת on purpose. For שבת, such a divider does not split the area into separate fields.
steps.whatToRemember: From רבין's wording, a מצר or חצב divides fields for פאה and טומאה, but not for שבת. רבא disagrees in the next step.

phrases.english: But for Shabbat, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבין's statement and limits it after the טומאה case has been explained
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבין's wording, a מצר or חצב divides fields for פאה and טומאה only, not for שבת. רבא disputes this.

steps.title: רבא: The divider counts even for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a מצר or חצב divides an area into separate parts even for the laws of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: It divides even for the laws of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with the conclusion of Step 5 and says the divider works for שבת too. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the divider counts only for פאה and טומאה. רבא widens this and adds שבת to the list. So the same strip of land would split an area into two separate places for שבת as well.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a different view here

phrases.english: Rava says:
Even with regard to the matter of Shabbat,
phrases.notes: He means the מצר or חצב from Step 5 also counts as a divider for שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 5's limit and extends the divider to שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצר or חצב separates areas even for the laws of שבת.

steps.title: The ברייתא about carrying two halves of a fig
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: carrying two half-fig amounts makes a person liable if both were done in one period of forgetting, and exempt if done in two separate periods.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: If someone carried half a dried fig into רשות הרבים and put it down, and then carried out another half, he is liable if it all happened in one period of forgetting. If it happened in two separate periods of forgetting, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts quoting a ברייתא to support his view. This first part gives the basic case and the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You need a full fig's size to be liable for carrying on שבת. Two halves join together only if the person did not remember in between that this is forbidden. If he remembered in between, the two acts stay separate, and each one is too small to count.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A dried fig, the minimum size for carrying food on שבת
A period of forgetting, when the person does not know it is שבת or that the act is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: "One העלם" does not mean one act. It means one stretch of time with no remembering in between. Two acts can happen inside one העלם.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who carried out half a dried fig
into the public domain and placed it there,
and then went back and carried out another half of a dried fig;
if within one lapse of awareness, he is liable.
If within two lapses of awareness, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that will support רבא's claim
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a divider counts for שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about carrying two half-fig amounts on שבת

steps.title: רבי יוסי's opinion begins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts רבי יוסי's view about the case where everything happened in one period of forgetting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If it was in one period of forgetting...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins quoting רבי יוסי. His sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי takes up the case the first opinion called liable, one period of forgetting. He is about to add a further detail to that case. That detail is where רבא's proof will come from.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds a further detail to the case
The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If within one lapse of awareness,
phrases.notes: His sentence isn't finished yet. The rest of his words come on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second opinion
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a divider counts for שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's opinion in the ברייתא, which continues on the next amud
